description:
## The gap

`lib/enum.fz` has no `@moduledoc`, and 34 of its 63 public functions have no `@doc`: `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `sort`, `take`, `drop`, `each`, `split`, `all?`, `any?`, `count`, `member?`, `find`, `scan`, `with_index` and the rest. The 33 docs that do exist all landed in the module's later half, and each is a single sentence.

## What the docs should be

Elixir's shape: a summary line, a paragraph on the behaviour that matters, and an `## Examples` section. That needs heredocs to attach to `@doc`, which is why this waits on that work.

Write for the reader who has the function in front of them and needs to know what it answers at the edges -- what an empty enumerable gives, what a negative count means, which end a duplicate survives at, whether order is encounter order or term order.

## Acceptance

- Every public function carries a `@doc`, and the module carries a `@moduledoc`.
- Each doc states the result for the empty enumerable where that is not obvious.
- No ticket numbers, no capitals for emphasis, no re-justification against Elixir beyond the one note in the `@moduledoc`.

comments.text: Delivered by 4d5285826 (fz-5xp.97): lib/enum.fz now carries a @moduledoc and 77 @doc blocks across its 62 distinct public function names, each with a verified ## Examples block. Note this landed BEFORE .83's re-layout rather than after, so the docs will move with the functions when .83 runs; nothing needs rewriting, only relocating.

title: Enum: document every public function
